
4d-Block Quadruple-Zeta Basis Set Archive
=========================================


Date: 22 Jun 2006


When publishing work that uses these basis sets, please use the following citation:

K.G. Dyall, in preparation. Available from the Dirac web site, http://dirac.chem.sdu.dk.



This archive contains the exponents and the SCF spinor or orbital coefficients, 
given with respect to normalized (spherical or 2-spinor) Gaussian functions, for
the quadruple-zeta basis sets described in the above article.  The contractions include
the 5p orbital and are taken from SCF calculations on the configuration average 
of the following configurations:

For Y, Zr, Tc: d^n s^2, d^n+1 s^1, and d^n p^2 configurations in a 6:3:1 ratio. 
For Nb, Mo, Ru, Rh, Ag: d^n s^2, d^n+1 s^1, and d^n p^2 configurations in a 3:6:1 ratio. 
For Cd: d^n s^2 and d^n p^2 configurations in a 9:1 ratio. 

The archive is set out as follows.

1. Exponents and SCF coefficients for Dirac-Hartree-Fock wave functions, in order
   of Z. The large component functions are given first, followed by the small 
   component functions. Both components are labelled with the large component
   symmetry type, but the primitive functions for the small component are
   those obtained by restricted kinetic balance from the large component.
   The spin-orbit components have a "-" label for j=l-1/2 and a "+" label for
   j=l+1/2.

2. Exponents and SCF coefficients for spin-free modified Dirac-Hartree-Fock wave
   functions, in order of Z. The large component functions are given first, 
   followed by the pseudo-large component functions, then the Foldy-Wouthuysen
   transformed large component functions. Note that all components have the same
   symmetry type. 

3. Exponents of valence correlating functions.

4. Exponents of 4d polarizing functions.

5. Exponents of 4s4p core correlating functions.

6. Exponents of 3d correlating functions; these are supplied in the unlikely
   event that the 3d needs to be correlated.


Basis set construction.
----------------------


Contracted basis sets can be constructed by adding primitive functions to the SCF 
set. These basis sets are described below. Note that the term "quadruple zeta" applies 
to the s and p set; the d set is sextuple zeta. This is a result of keeping a reasonable 
energy balance for the basis sets. 

NOTE: Functions are counted from the function with the smallest exponent to the function
      with the largest exponent.

The valence space is defined here as the 4d, 5s, and 5p orbitals. 


1. Valence flexibility. To the SCF functions, add the following:

   1st, 2nd, and 4th s primitives from the SCF set 
   2nd, 3rd, and 4th p primitives from the SCF set
   1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th d primitives from the SCF set
   Correlating 3f2g1h functions

2. Valence + outer core. This set adds the outer-core correlation from the 4s and 4p
   shells. To set 1, add the following functions:

   5th, 6th, and 8th s primitives from the SCF set 
   5th, 6th, and 8th p primitives from the SCF set
   5th, 6th, and 7th d primitives from the SCF set
   For Y, 4s4p correlating 2f functions
   For Zr, inner f from the 4s4p correlating set
   For Y - Rh, 4s4p correlating g function

   The 2f1g set for the remaining elements is well covered by the 4d5s correlating set.
   If linear dependence is encountered in the d set, do not uncontract the 1st primitive.

3. Dipole polarization of the 4d. To any of the above basis sets, add the polarizing
   f, g, and h functions.





Dirac-Hartree-Fock basis sets           
=============================
